# Cave Echoes: your own sounds

Put sound files in this folder to hear the demo with them. Every file is optional: when one is missing, the demo makes
a simple stand-in for it, so it always runs.

Each name below can end in `.ogg`, `.wav`, `.flac` or `.mp3` (tried in that order). To keep the sounds somewhere else,
start the demo with that folder as its command line, for example `cave-echoes.exe "D:\Sounds\Cave"`.
When the demo is run straight from the compiler (`blitzcc cave-echoes.bb`, without `-o`), it finds this folder
next to the `.bb` file.

| File | Where it plays | Loops | Tips |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `campfire` | The campfire in front of the cave, in 3D | Yes | Mono. Crackles make the occlusion easy to hear. |
| `cave-drip` | Dripping water at the back of the cave, in 3D | Yes | Mono. A few drops with quiet in between, so the reverb tail is heard. |
| `river` | The river at the bottom of the hill, in 3D | Yes | Mono. Bright, hissing water shows the air absorption best. |
| `wind` | Everywhere outside, fades away inside the cave | Yes | Stereo is fine. It should loop without a seam. |
| `footstep` | Each step the player takes | No | Short and dry, about 0.1 to 0.3 seconds. |
| `clap` | When the player claps (E or the left mouse button) | No | Short and sharp, with no reverb of its own, so the cliff echo and the cave reverb stand out. |

The 3D sounds (campfire, cave-drip, river) should be mono: they are placed in the world, and a stereo file can't be.
The demo plays every file as it is, so set the loudness of the files against each other before you put them here.
